correctness.rationale: Completing the square in the two mixed products shifts the Gaussian centers by ±(q-p)T/[2(p+q)]. The Fourier phases therefore combine into cos(κTω) with positive prefactor 2c sqrt(2π/(p+q)) exp[-(pqT²+ω²)/(2(p+q))]. The diagonal products give the two stated positive exponential ratios. The axes are strictly positive. Outside either separated sector one ratio grows exponentially in T²+ω² uniformly, ruling out distant zeros. On an interior ray the ratios and their derivatives decay exponentially in t=T². Disjoint fixed neighborhoods of the cosine nodes have a derivative bounded away from zero and opposite signs at the ends for late nodes; the complement has no late roots. The first-order Taylor equation gives the stated (-1)^k sign and quadratic remainder, and real analyticity and positivity at t=0 rule out infinitely many early roots. Counting nodes gives the stated O(1) error. Choosing progressively more distant roots on interior slopes tending to either boundary gives sharpness even when that boundary ray has no zeros. On a boundary ray one ratio is a positive constant, so its being below one is necessary and sufficient for sign changes at late oscillations; equality leaves a strictly positive decaying term. On the balanced ray the ratios add to B exp(-δt), with B>1 by AM–GM. There can be no root before log(B)/δ, and the next cosine minimum supplies the other bracket endpoint, including equality. At q=p+ε, δ~ε²/(8p), β~ε/4; for c≠1 their time scales are separated and B tends to (c+c⁻¹)/2. At c=1, log B=3ε²/(32p²)+O(ε³), whereas πδ/β is of order ε. In phase coordinates the function is uniformly positive away from π on the first half-cycle and strictly negative at π for small ε, giving the asserted 4π limit. The degenerate Gaussian is zero-free. No extension to general mixtures, shifted centers, or all finite zero components is proved.

The uploaded output is finite and was inspected, not rerun. Its balanced-ray root finder does not certify firstness from a sign bracket alone; the next-minimum proof gives a global bound for the first root without needing that numerical assertion. Independent spot checks integrated on [-10,10] by composite Simpson with 4096 subintervals at (p,q,c,T,ω)=(0.8,3.1,1.4,1.3,2.05), matching 1.615901612046245 to roundoff. An independent floating-point first-root check scanned negative cosine lobes from the amplitude threshold, located their minima using convexity there, and bisected on the decreasing side of the first feasible lobe. At p=2 and ε=0.01,0.001,0.0001 the scaled values were 12.07626,12.40888,12.51634 for c=1, and 8.41266,8.18059,8.17442 for c=3. These finite checks are not proofs of the quantified limits.

value.rationale: This natural positive-window model separates pointwise positivity of the window and its Fourier transform from positivity of the ambiguity function. The exact allowed escape directions, endpoint-amplitude cuts and sharp ray census tell where nulls persist, while the two asymptotic scales explain quantitatively how nulls disappear in the approach to a single zero-free Gaussian. These are useful geometric and singular-perturbation conclusions beyond plotting the known interference pattern.
